Mathematical Models  A large variety of real-world situations can be described using mathematical models. A mathematical model is a  method of simulating real-life situations with mathematical equations. Physicists, engineers, economists, and other  researchers develop models by combining observation with quantitative data to develop equations, functions, graphs,  and other mathematical tools to describe the behavior of various systems accurately. Models are useful because they  help predict future outcomes. Examples of mathematical models include the study of population dynamics,  investigations of weather patterns, and predictions of product sales.
